hook: A 143-page Department of War compilation file dated January 9, 1950, collecting incident reports on 'Flying Discs' observed during 1949, filed by military and Civilian Aviation Authority witnesses under Flight Service Regulation 200-4. The pymupdf extraction captured no readable text — only a declassification header — indicating the pages are scanned images that were not OCR-processed.
why_it_matters: This file represents early institutionalized UFO reporting within the military bureaucracy, predating Project Blue Book and operating under the Department of War designation (which was being reorganized into the DoD during this period). The inclusion of MATS and AACS message traffic alongside a Japanese weather station report suggests multi-theater data collection at a time when the Air Force was actively debating whether 'flying discs' were Soviet technology, natural phenomena, or something else. The FSR 200-4 compliance framework indicates this was part of a structured, mandatory reporting chain — not ad hoc collection.
key_findings: The document was compiled under FSR 200-4 (1948 Flight Service Regulation), establishing that UFO reporting was a codified military requirement by 1948, not voluntary.
Witness sources include both military personnel and Civilian Aviation Authority (CAA) observers, indicating the reporting net extended to civil aviation infrastructure.

Military Air Transport Service (MATS) and Army Airways Communications System (AACS) message traffic is included, suggesting real-time radio intercepts or dispatches were folded into the incident file.
A report from a weather station in Japan is included, placing at least one incident in the Pacific theater during the early occupation period.

The file contains diagrams, which — given the era and subject — likely depict observed object shapes or flight paths, though the text extraction was entirely unsuccessful and no diagram content is recoverable from this extraction.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This 1949 'Flying Discs' compilation is a direct predecessor to Project Blue Book, operating under the same FSR 200-4 reporting framework that fed into the formal Blue Book investigation structure.

Wright-Patterson AFB was the institutional home for Air Force UFO investigation files in this period; MATS and military intelligence reports of this type were processed through commands headquartered there.
Multi-theater incident reports with military intelligence content from 1949-1950 were the type of material that fed into CIA's early UAP assessments, including the 1952 Robertson Panel inputs.
